paragraphs.dominant_move: says at the beginning of the research we need to define the health of the higher education system
says we search the relevant reports of the European Union, UNESCO and OECD
says combined with some basic concepts of educational economics we divide the health status into two aspects
says one is the status quo of industry performance, the other is the improvement potential
says in many comprehensive evaluation models we choose TOPSIS to build our evaluation model
says considering the disadvantage that AHP relies too much on the supervisor's judgment we decide to use the entropy weight method
says through the combination method we transform two sets of qualitative evaluation system into a quantitative evaluation model
says we select the data of 21 OECD member countries in 2016 and put them into two sets of evaluation models
says 11 countries performed well in the performance status quo while 10 countries performed well in the improvement potential
says we selected Chile because of its huge improvement potential and relatively poor performance status
says we firstly analyzed the differences between Chile and other countries in various indicators
says then we formulated a reasonable and sustainable vision for Chile based on its national conditions
says before proposing the policy we use the data published by the Ministry of Education to verify the necessity of strong policies
says between the status quo and vision we put forward policies suitable for Chile's higher education system and the timeline for its implementation
says although the policy we recommend can significantly improve the performance status we still cannot call the system healthy
says therefore the effectiveness of the policy we proposed is not sufficient
says finally we discuss the impact of the implementation of the policy and the advantages and disadvantages of this study
says the scope of contemporary higher education is very wide
says whether to have a healthy and sustainable higher education system is also a topic of concern to people
says in recent years the proportion of young people gaining higher education qualifications has been on the rise
says while young graduates enjoy a large premium in earnings the employment premium they enjoy has remained relatively stable
says at the same time the cost of higher education is higher than that of other levels and the expenditure is increasing rapidly
says in addition high non-completion rates and poor course quality lead to delayed completion
says in the post-epidemic era the higher education system is in urgent need of reform
says the old system is bound to fail to adapt to the changing times
says how to achieve a more healthy and sustainable system is a fundamental issue that all countries need to reflect on and face
says how to construct a set of appropriate models to correctly evaluate, appraise and improve a country's system is a problem we are facing
says then we will further select the countries that need to improve and provide them with reasonable policy recommendations
says so as to achieve the reasonable vision we have drawn for them in the right time
says of course the effectiveness of the policy and the impact of policy changes on the real world still need further evaluation

global_organization_chain: Define health before choosing a method, and split it into present performance and future potential
Reject a flattering indicator and a subjective weighting method, each for a named reason
Score 21 countries twice and pick the one where the scores disagree most
Set the target at the mean, and only for indicators whose mean is representative
Show the untouched trend missing the target, then show the target itself still short of healthy

main_argument_chains.claim: Chile's higher education is weak now and has the most room to improve, and even a vision set at the international mean leaves it short of healthy.
support_steps: Separate health from strength, and performance from potential
Score both with entropy-weighted TOPSIS on 21 OECD countries
Find Chile at 0.279 on performance and 0.734 on potential, the widest gap
Keep only the four indicators whose variation is small, and take their means as the vision
Forecast the master ratio to 2028 and show a 46 percent rise that misses the mean
Substitute the vision and rescore: 0.279 rises to 0.445, still the fair band
Say the policy is not sufficient
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Raise government investment, supervise and consolidate private institutions, move the system out of profit, and temporarily relax graduate enrollment, while treating epidemic control as outside the paper.

warnings.warning: Every formula on pages 12 and 13 is printed with private-use glyphs, and the source file is not valid UTF-8. The steps were reconstructed as standard entropy weighting and TOPSIS. The prose also reverses the entropy logic, and it dates Shannon's 1948 paper to 1984.
The GM(1,1) response formula is not legible. The model name, the passed level-ratio test, the 2007-2018 window and the 46 percent rise are readable and were kept.
